used.source: Volume 1 — the spies and the giants

candidates.summary: Abraham welcomes three visitors, serves them generously, and Sarah hears the surprising promise that she will have a son.
Abraham’s servant prays for guidance, and Rebekah responds with extraordinary kindness by drawing water for him and his camels.
While Jacob sleeps on his journey, God gives him a dream of a stairway to heaven and repeats the covenant promise.
Joseph faithfully serves two imprisoned officials and, giving God the credit, explains their dreams and their different outcomes.
Moses is hidden in a basket among the reeds, where Pharaoh’s daughter finds him and his own mother is chosen to nurse him.
God provides manna each morning for Israel in the wilderness and teaches the people to gather only what each household needs.
Israel prevails against Amalek while Moses holds up his hands, with Aaron and Hur supporting him when he grows tired.
The priests step into the flooded Jordan carrying the ark, the water stops, and all Israel crosses on dry ground.
Deborah delivers God’s message to Barak, accompanies him in faith, and Israel is given victory over Sisera’s stronger army.
Ruth refuses to abandon Naomi and chooses to go with her to Bethlehem, showing loyal love during grief and uncertainty.
Young Samuel hears God calling at night, learns from Eli how to listen, and faithfully delivers the message he receives.
God sends Samuel to Jesse’s family and chooses David, the overlooked youngest son, teaching that God looks at the heart.
David trusts God, refuses Saul’s armor, and defeats the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone.
King David seeks out Mephibosheth, restores his family land, and welcomes him permanently at the royal table.
God cares for exhausted Elijah, then meets him at Horeb not in wind, earthquake, or fire but in a gentle whisper.
Naaman reluctantly follows Elisha’s simple instruction to wash in the Jordan and is healed, learning humility and acknowledging God.
Elisha’s servant sees God’s heavenly army, and captured enemy soldiers are fed and released instead of being killed.
Four hungry men discover that the enemy camp has been abandoned and hurry back to share the good news with a starving city.
Nehemiah quietly inspects Jerusalem’s broken walls, then invites the people to rebuild despite ridicule from their opponents.
The people continue rebuilding Jerusalem’s wall through mockery and threats, working together while staying watchful and trusting God.
Daniel and his friends respectfully request food that honors their convictions, and God gives them health, wisdom, and understanding.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image, and God preserves them in the blazing furnace.
Daniel continues praying despite the royal decree, is thrown among lions, and God shuts the lions’ mouths through the night.
Jonah runs from God, is rescued through a great fish, preaches to Nineveh, and learns about God’s compassion for others.
Jesus receives a crowd with compassion and feeds more than five thousand people from five loaves and two fish.
Jesus walks across the stormy water, Peter steps out toward him, and Jesus rescues Peter when fear overtakes him.
After an empty night of fishing, Simon follows Jesus’ instruction and receives an overwhelming catch before being called to follow him.
Jesus tells of a Samaritan who compassionately rescues an injured stranger after others have passed by without helping.
Jesus describes a shepherd who searches for one lost sheep and celebrates when he carries it safely home.
Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus, welcomes him joyfully, and responds by making generous restitution for his wrongdoing.
At a wedding in Cana, Jesus quietly turns water into wine, revealing his glory and strengthening his disciples’ faith.
Jesus heals a man born blind, who steadily speaks the truth about what happened despite repeated questioning and pressure.
Jesus grieves with Martha and Mary, then calls Lazarus out of the tomb and reveals his authority over death.
Peter and John meet a man unable to walk at the temple gate, and Jesus heals him so he enters praising God.
Philip follows God’s direction to a desert road, explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian official, and baptizes him after he believes.
Jesus stops Saul on the road to Damascus, and Ananias courageously visits him so Saul receives sight and is baptized.
Paul encourages everyone during a violent shipwreck, the sailors follow wise instructions, and all aboard reach shore alive.
